The relevant row is "Outpatient diagnostic tests and therapeutic services and supplies" on pages 52–55. Outpatient hospital services on pages 57–58 repeat some of the same costs. Quotes must occur exactly once on their page, so I read the table columns down and joined them.

I did not include the "Diagnostic Procedures and Tests" and "Other outpatient diagnostic tests" costs, because the document does not tie them to a named benefit. Screening and dental X-rays are out of scope.

Advanced imaging is priced together as one "Advanced Imaging Services" line, and the document defines it as CT, MRI, MRA and PET "or other similar technology." That is not exactly CT, MRI and PET, so I give separate facts for ct, mri and pet with the same quotes. Basic radiological services I map to imaging.xray.

Quotes on page 53 read one column down. "Advanced Imaging Services $330 copayment – PCP's Office – Specialist's Office" is contiguous, so it works as a quote. For page 57, the outpatient hospital lines are contiguous, for example "Advanced Imaging Services $345 copayment – Outpatient Hospital". That string occurs once on page 57, so I used page 57 for the outpatient hospital advanced imaging, nuclear and basic radiological costs.

Page 53 quotes for office and freestanding costs:
- Advanced imaging in the PCP and specialist offices is $330.
- Advanced imaging at a freestanding facility is $205. The quote "$205 copayment – Freestanding Radiological Facility" is unique on page 53.
- Basic radiology costs $0 at the PCP, $40 at the specialist and freestanding facility, and $145 at an outpatient hospital.

Out-of-network costs on page 55 and page 58 are 50% coinsurance for advanced imaging and basic radiology in all settings. The advanced imaging lines on page 55 list four settings together, so I give a fact per setting with the same quote. Page 58 gives the outpatient hospital lines. Because "Advanced Imaging Services 50% coinsurance" repeats on page 55, I use the longer quote with the settings.

Nuclear medicine is $325 at an outpatient hospital or freestanding facility in network (page 54), and 50% out of network (page 55).

Diagnostic mammography is $0 in the specialist's office, outpatient hospital and freestanding facility, both in and out of network (pages 53 and 55).
